newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi ports generated $320 mln in revenue in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Saudi ports generated $320 mln in revenue in 1996.

text.p: Saudi Arabian ports generated 1.2 billion riyals ($320 million) in revenue in 1996 from higher imports, the kingdom's top ports official said on Tuesday.

Saudi Arabia's ports authority (SEAPA) head Mohammed Bakr also said the kingdom planned to lease plots of land at the eastern port of Dammam to companies for 10 years as part of a wider plan to boost re-exports from the oil-rich kingdom.
"This is the first stage of a comprehensive plan to activate Saudi Arabia's re-exports programme. It will cover other ports later", he said.
"Revenue from ports in the first quarter of this year rose by 25 percent over the same period last year," he told a meeting of Saudi chambers of trade and commerce leaders.

Bakr gave no figures for the ports' 1996 profits but said all Saudi ports -- six main commercial and two industrial -- were covering the cost of their operations. Profits in 1995 stood at 558 million riyals.

Bakr and the local businessmen explored investment opportunities provided under a recent Saudi decision to let the private sector take over operations, maintenance and management of docks and equipment used by SEAPA.
All operations would be run on a commercial basis.
SEAPA last week chose a local company to run a terminal handling imports of bulk wheat at Jeddah port. It would invest in machinery to handle five million tonnes of wheat a year.
SEAPA said last month it had shortlisted 43 private firms to bid for six projects under the gradual scheme to upgrade its port infrastructure and boost handling capabilities.
Under the gradual privatisation plan, SEAPA would retain its supervisory role over the ports on the Red Sea and Gulf coasts and ensure there were no new price rises in handling fees.

The six projects include cargo terminals at the eastern ports of Damman and Jubail, a roll-on roll-off (ro-ro) goods terminal at Jeddah and the management of King Fahd ship repair complex, the official said.
He said SEAPA had no plans to invest in new port terminals, but wanted to increase their efficiency and the percentage of utilised capacity.
Jeddah alone handles nearly one million containers a year, making it the kingdom's busiest port.
